I'll start by fixing conventions and sampling the blade sections numerically, before any CAD: axis = z, tangential coordinate t = rθ, stagger measured from axial.

```python
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ---- parameters (metres). From the request unless marked ASSUMED ----
R_HUB, R_TIP = 0.045, 0.090
NB          = 28
CHORD       = 0.022
THICK       = 0.06          # max thickness / chord
STAG_ROOT   = np.radians(30.0)
TWIST       = np.radians(35.0)   # extra stagger at tip
CAMBER      = np.radians(40.0)   # ASSUMED total camber (turning) angle, circular-arc camber line
PITCH_ANG   = 2*np.pi/NB

def stagger(r):
    return STAG_ROOT + TWIST*(r-R_HUB)/(R_TIP-R_HUB)

def section(r, n=81):
    """blade section in (z_axial, t_tangential) at radius r; also camber line."""
    c = CHORD
    Rc = (c/2)/np.sin(CAMBER/2)
    beta = np.linspace(0, np.pi, n)
    x = c*(1-np.cos(beta))/2                      # cosine spacing 0..c
    yc = np.sqrt(Rc**2-(x-c/2)**2) - np.sqrt(Rc**2-(c/2)**2)
    dyc = -(x-c/2)/np.sqrt(Rc**2-(x-c/2)**2)
    phi = np.arctan(dyc)
    xx = x/c
    yt = 5*THICK*c*(0.2969*np.sqrt(xx)-0.1260*xx-0.3516*xx**2+0.2843*xx**3-0.1036*xx**4)
    up = np.array([x-yt*np.sin(phi), yc+yt*np.cos(phi)])
    lo = np.array([x+yt*np.sin(phi), yc-yt*np.cos(phi)])
    cam= np.array([x, yc])
    chi = stagger(r); Rm = np.array([[np.cos(chi),-np.sin(chi)],[np.sin(chi),np.cos(chi)]])
    sh  = np.array([[c/2],[0.0]])
    return [Rm@(a-sh) for a in (up, lo, cam)]

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1,3, figsize=(13,4.5))
for ax, r in zip(axs, [R_HUB, (R_HUB+R_TIP)/2, R_TIP]):
    up, lo, cam = section(r)
    p = PITCH_ANG*r
    ax.plot(up[0]*1e3, up[1]*1e3, 'b'); ax.plot(lo[0]*1e3, lo[1]*1e3, 'r')
    ax.plot(cam[0]*1e3, cam[1]*1e3,'k--')
    for s in (-p/2, p/2):
        ax.plot(cam[0]*1e3, (cam[1]+s)*1e3, 'g-')
    ax.set_title(f"r={r*1e3:.0f}mm  stagger={np.degrees(stagger(r)):.0f}deg pitch={p*1e3:.1f}mm")
    ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.grid(alpha=.3); ax.set_xlabel('z [mm]'); ax.set_ylabel('t [mm]')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig('sections.png', dpi=90)
for r in [R_HUB, 0.0675, R_TIP]:
    up,lo,cam = section(r)
    print(f"r={r*1e3:5.1f} chordproj_z={(up[0].max()-up[0].min())*1e3:5.2f} "
          f"t_extent={(up[1].max()-lo[1].min())*1e3:5.2f} pitch_t={PITCH_ANG*r*1e3:5.2f} "
          f"maxthick_meas={np.max(np.hypot(up[0]-lo[0],up[1]-lo[1]))*1e3:.3f}")
print('sections.png')
```

Thickness checks out (1.320 mm = 6% × 22 mm). Note the root section spans 11.0 mm tangentially against a 10.1 mm pitch — blades overlap, so the periodic surfaces must follow the camber line (offset ± half pitch), not be flat θ = const planes. Let me look at the sections.

Sections look right. Now the CAD plan: periodic surfaces follow the camber line offset by ±half-pitch (with axial extensions), so the blade sits clear inside the passage block. Let me check the build123d API pieces I need.

Now the blade solid: loft of closed section wires (two spline edges each — suction and pressure — so the loft has exactly two lateral faces I can name), wrapped onto cylinders, extended slightly past hub and shroud.
The loft ran but reported invalid with only 2 faces — I need to re-emit it as one accepted cell and inspect it properly.
The loft has no end caps. I'll cap the two radial ends with filled surfaces and sew into a closed solid.
Blade solid is valid; section area 20.0 mm² matches the analytic NACA area for 6% × 22 mm. Now the passage block, whose periodic walls follow the camber line offset by ± half pitch.
Block is right: the two periodic faces are 12.857° apart = 360/28, and the volume matches the analytic annular-sector volume (43.0 cm³). Now cut the blade out.
Volume matches exactly. Faces 6 and 7 are the blade; I classify them as suction/pressure by testing sampled surface points against the analytic upper/lower section curves, not by position in a box.
Hub/shroud came out as plate surfaces (com radius 44.6 mm — sagging), not exact cylinders. Fix: loft the block past both radii and intersect with a true annulus, then mesh immediately.
Now classify all eight faces and export the solid for meshing.
Re-emitting the classifier with all its helpers defined inside, so the script is self-contained.
Coarse tet mesh in gmsh, with surfaces matched to my labels by centre of mass.
Stray `setNumbers` line; removing it and re-running.
Coarse mesh exists. Now convert to OpenFOAM and check it.
checkMesh passes on the coarse mesh (max skew 0.99, max non-orth 67.9). Let me look at it before refining.
pyvista can't read .msh directly. I'll export one STL per patch from the mesh itself (conformal by construction) and view those.
Let me render each patch separately to verify identity, viewed along the axis.
Patches are all in the right place. Now measure the requested quantities from the built solid itself.
Chord 22.01 mm, stagger 30.0°/64.8° (twist 34.8°). The banded thickness estimate is unreliable; measuring it properly as min distance between the two blade surfaces.
Root figure looks wrong — probably sparse sampling in the band. Let me plot the sampled root band to see.
Sampling is too sparse for nearest-point; measuring instead as distance to the ordered polyline of the opposite surface.
Thickness ~6.1–6.7% (overestimate from coarse polylines; exact generating value 1.320 mm = 6.00%). Now refine the mesh and re-check.
336k tets, checkMesh OK (max non-orth 70.4 on 1 face, max skewness 0.985). Re-exporting patch STLs at this resolution and a final look.
